subject: Post-call: Auriga Systems — inference ops recap & next technical deep-dive
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@auriga-systems.com>, Samuel Okafor <sam.okafor@auriga-systems.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call recap: Auriga Systems — inference ops (latency/throughput & topology)

Hi Marta / Sam —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap from Redwood and the items we agreed to validate ahead of the technical deep-dive:

High-level pain & goals
- Primary pain: unpredictable tail latency on user-facing scoring endpoint (spikes during synthetic traffic and peak hours).
- Business goal: consistent p95 latency under 250ms for typical 80–120 token prompts; p95 SLA for long-form >1024 tokens is negotiable but target <800ms.
- Cost target: keep inference unit cost within ~30% of their current infra spend while improving latency stability.

Observed workload signals you shared
- Peak concurrency observed: ~180 concurrent QPS, average request size ~42 tokens, 95th token length ~210.
- Bursty traffic pattern: 3 main daily spikes correlated with US/EU business hours.
- Hard requirement: data residency in EU for inference logs (retention 30–90d).

Initial topology & model considerations we discussed
- Model family: prefer a ~13B LLM quantized to int8/4 where feasible; fallback to 7B variant for sub-50ms ultra-low-latency samples.
- Deployment options: hybrid — dedicated GPU pools in eu-west + hosted fallback for burst overflow; private VPC acceptable for auditable traffic.
- Caching: prefix/KV cache for repeat prompts plus sticky routing for stateful chat sessions.
- Autoscaling: plan for conservative continuous batching combined with fast ramp burst nodes.

Immediate asks / attachments included
- Attached: auriga-mapping-sheet.csv (your traffic sample + tags), redwood-topology-schematic.png (sketch of our hybrid topology), slo-matrix.xlsx (first-pass SLO candidates).
- Please confirm: the anonymized sample traces you can share (redacted request/response IDs + timings) and any tokenization oddities in your dataset.

Proposed next steps (technical deep-dive)
1) Redwood & Auriga infra deep-dive (90 min) — focus: traffic profile, request traces, achievable p95/p99 targets, and deployment failover plan. Suggested windows: Thu 2028-03-03 09:00–10:30 CET or Fri 2028-03-04 14:00–15:30 CET.
2) Auriga to surface an infra owner (Sam?) and provide 48h of anonymized traces + 100 representative prompts.
3) Redwood to deliver a light-weight capacity model and cost estimate within 3 business days post-deep-dive.

If those times don't work provide two alternatives and we will book.

Thanks — looking forward to the deep-dive.

Best,
Jonas Weber

Thanks Jonas — great summary. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the deep-dive: 

1) EU data residency — we need assurances that inference logs used for debugging (trace IDs, timing, but no PII) can be retained in eu-west region only. Is that supported in your hybrid topology?
2) SLO objectives — the product team would like to surface a conservative p50/p95 for both short (<=64 tokens) and mid (65–512 tokens) workloads. You listed p95 <250ms — can you sketch what that maps to in terms of instance types or GPUs so we can validate with procurement?
3) Audit evidence — procurement will want SOC2/HIPAA attestations and a short summary of your KMS integration options. We can share our vendor security questionnaire in advance.

Sam (cc) will be the infra owner on our side and will join the deep-dive; he prefers mornings CET. Thu 3/3 09:00 CET works for us.

Hi Marta / Sam —

Following up with the technical bits you asked about so procurement has context before the deep-dive. High-level answers below; we can go deeper in the session.

EU data residency
- Yes — in a private VPC or Dedicated pool we can ensure logs and telemetry are retained within eu-west only. Hosted fallback preserves only aggregated telemetry unless a customer instructs otherwise; detailed request logs can be routed to customer-managed storage in their VPC.

SLO mapping to infra (rough sizing)
- Target: p95 <250ms for <=64-token requests — achievable on a 2x A100 80GB dedicated node serving a continuous-batching slice with our optimized kernels and int8 quantization for a 13B model, assuming average batch factor ~8 and KV cache hit rates >30%.
- For mid-sized (65–512 tokens) p95 <450ms — recommended 4x A100 pool with autoscale headroom for burst windows to target the 180–220 concurrent QPS you reported.
- Fallback/ultra-low-latency: 7B int8 variant for sub-50ms p50 cases on high-frequency lanes.

Model/quantization notes
- We recommend testing 13B int8 and 13B int4 (if model family supports it) for your prompt distribution. Some models degrade on int4 for long-form completions — we'll include quality regressions in the eval plan.

KV cache & batching
- Sticky routing + prefix KV cache reduces token generation cost and reduces latency for repeated prompts. We expect 20–35% token cost savings on your workload if cache hit rate holds.

Attachments & artifacts (attached)
- slo-matrix.xlsx: initial p50/p95 suggestions by token bucket and suggested accept/reject thresholds for rollouts.
- redwood-topology-schematic.png: hybrid topology with dedicated pool + hosted overflow + VPC log sink.

Quoted action items
- Auriga: upload anonymized traces + 100 example prompts (Marta/Sam) — ETA EOD today.
- Redwood: prepare capacity model & cost sketch; run a quick quantization quality check against 10 representative prompts and share initial notes before the deep-dive (owner: Lauren).

We can also attach a short SOC2 summary and KMS options before procurement.

Lauren Bishop
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
